title: A search for cold molecular outflows in cosmic-noon galaxies
question: Do typical main-sequence star-forming galaxies at cosmic noon (z_med~1.3) show cold molecular gas extended to CGM scales or broad CO(2-1) wings indicating molecular outflows, via stacking of ALMA Band 3 CO(2-1) data compared with Ks-band stellar emission

data.sensitivity: average 0.60 mJy/beam per 30 km/s channel (0.73 mJy/beam for the 5 multi-execution galaxies)

what.value: CO(2-1) observations description and per-galaxy stellar mass, infrared luminosity and SFR measurements for the sample

evidence.quote: for a complete report of the observations
stellar mass and infrared luminosity measurements

what.value: Ks-band PSF information used to build the 2D Moffat PSF model (UltraVISTA / ESO programme 179.A-2005)

evidence.quote: to compute a 2D PSF Moffat model with FWHM

recipe.method: Take the S/N>=3 CO(2-1) detections from the 75-SFG ALMA programme, remove a merger and galaxies without stellar mass, leaving 26 galaxies
uv-plane continuum subtraction then tclean imaging with natural weighting and 30 km/s channels, homogeneously for all galaxies
key_parameters: continuum polynomial order 0; natural weighting; 30 km/s channels

recipe.goal: Extract each galaxy spectrum and fit a Gaussian
recipe.method: Extract spectrum in a 2 arcsec radius aperture at the cube centre, perturb it by its 1 sigma noise, fit a Gaussian, repeat 500 times and take the median fit

recipe.goal: Build moment-0 maps and stack them
recipe.method: Make intensity maps over +/-FWHM of the best Gaussian with immoments, realign each map to its emission peak, and take the uniform (unweighted) mean; the stacked synthesised beam is computed the same way
key_parameters: uniform weights w_n=1; noise-weighted stack gave very similar results

recipe.goal: Measure surface-brightness radial profiles of the stack
recipe.method: Mean flux normalised by the peak in annuli of 4 pixels width (~0.4 arcsec) out to 4 arcsec; error is the standard deviation within each annulus; same for the stacked beam
key_parameters: annulus width 4 pixels; profile out to 4 arcsec

recipe.goal: Deconvolve the beam and get intrinsic CO extent
recipe.method: Fit Sersic profiles to the CO and beam radial profiles (Re, Ie, n free); since n~0.5 for both, subtract the beam half-light radius in quadrature from the CO one
key_parameters: Re, Ie and Sersic index n free parameters
assumptions: Gaussian (n~0.5) profiles so analytical 1D Gaussian deconvolution applies
Cosmology H0=70, Om=0.3, OL=0.7 for converting arcsec to kpc

recipe.method: Align each cube in velocity to the Gaussian-fit peak and in position to the intensity-map peak, stack cubes (and beam cubes), then image moment 0 and compute radial profiles as before
Bin the sample by stellar mass, L_IR, sSFR (split at sample medians) and MS vs starburst (3.5 times above MS), stack radial profiles and spectra per bin

recipe.goal: Stack Ks-band images and compare with CO
recipe.method: Richardson-Lucy PSF deconvolution of each Ks image with a Moffat PSF, segmentation maps for source isolation and background subtraction, uniform stack, then compare radial profile with the intrinsic CO profile
Extract spectrum in a 2 arcsec aperture, fit a Gaussian, realign spectra to the fitted line centre, rebin to 60 km/s and uniformly stack
key_parameters: 2 arcsec aperture; 60 km/s rebinned channels (30 km/s version in appendix)

recipe.method: Fit single- and two-Gaussian models to the stacked spectrum and compare reduced chi-squared; a significantly better two-Gaussian fit would indicate outflowing material

answer_key.quantity: Noise level of stacked CO(2-1) intensity map

evidence.quote: The stacked intensity map has a noise level of 0.029 Jy/beam

answer_key.quantity: Peak S/N of stacked intensity map
Observed CO(2-1) emission extent in stack (r_max)
Sersic index of CO radial profile (n_CO)
Observed half-light radius of stacked CO (R_e,CO)
Half-light radius of stacked synthesised beam (R_e,beam)

evidence.quote: with a half-light radius of $R_e=5$ kpc
spatially extends to scales of $R_{\text{CO}}\sim12$ kpc
and a noise level of 0.11 mJy

answer_key.quantity: Reduced chi-squared, single vs two-Gaussian fit of stacked spectrum

not_stated_but_needed: Calibration route (pipeline vs manual), CASA pipeline version and flux calibrator/flux-scale handling for the 2016.1.00171.S data
tclean parameters: image size, cell size, deconvolver, niter/threshold, masking, restoring beam handling and whether maps are primary-beam corrected
Spectral window, rest frequency and line-free channel ranges used for uvcontsub and the cube frequency range
Which phase centre or position defines the 'centre of the cube' for the 2 arcsec aperture and how the peak is re-centred
Gaussian fit details (initial guesses, bounds, fit routine) and how the 1 sigma noise used for perturbations is measured
Two-Gaussian fit constraints (width and centre bounds, initial guesses) and the degrees of freedom used for reduced chi-squared
Sersic fit routine and weighting; how the normalisation by the peak and radial-profile centring are done
Richardson-Lucy iteration count and Ks cutout size, and the sigma-clipping/segmentation thresholds used in photutils
Number of galaxies per bin in the subsample stacks, and the exact IDs of the 5 multi-execution galaxies
missing_for_reproduction: tclean imaging parameters (image size, cell, masks, threshold, primary-beam handling)
Line-free channel selection and spectral setup used for uvcontsub
Fit initial guesses/bounds for single and two-Gaussian models and Sersic fits

score_reason: Public ALMA project and numeric results with a clear stacking recipe, but imaging, calibration and fit settings are not given and no code is released
rediscovery_reason: Data are public, the stacking and radial-profile recipe is mostly stated, and the main results (extent in kpc, Sersic parameters, line FWHM, chi-squared) are numeric
